items.title: Airbnb (ABNB): Is ABNB’s Strong Growth Story Already Priced Into the Stock?
items.summary: On August 7, 2026, Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) reported Q2 2026 results. items.title: Airbnb (ABNB) CEO Cuts Meetings In Half With AI Management Overhaul
items.summary: Airbnb (NasdaqGS:ABNB) CEO Brian Chesky is pushing a broad internal shift to use artificial intelligence across management workflows. Chesky is prioritising AI fluency for managers so routine decisions and coordination tasks can be handled by internal AI tools. The company is outlining plans to build more advanced AI agents aimed at automating complex cross‑team processes inside Airbnb. items.title: Uber Has Disappointed For More Than a Year: Here’s Why a Highly Respected Wall Street Firm Says It’s Going to Double
items.summary: Uber's stock has shed nearly 30% over the past year while its cash flow crossed $10 billion and analysts keep raising their targets. One highly respected Wall Street firm sees a path to doubling from here, and the reasoning goes well beyond the rideshare business you think you know.

items.title: How Low Could Expedia Stock Go If A Real Shock Follows This Slide?
items.summary: Expedia (EXPE) stock fell 7.7% on September 23, leaving it about 24% below its August 24 high of $339. Yet the company's latest results beat its forecast, and over the past 12 months the stock has still returned about 17%, roughly in line with the S&P 500. So how far could Expedia go in a real market shock.

items.title: Is Booking's Slowdown A Pause Or Its New Pace?
items.summary: Booking (BKNG) turns 35% of its sales into operating profit, against 18.6% for the S&P 500. Yet its stock lost 29% in the year to September 23, 2026, while the index returned 13%. Booking expects third-quarter 2026 revenue to grow just 4% to 6%. The question you face is whether that slower growth is a pause or Booking's new pace. Start with what the current price already asks you to pay.

items.title: Does The Move In Airbnb Stock Change Anything?
items.summary: Airbnb (ABNB) shares fell 21% in the month to September 23, while the S&P 500 rose 0.8%. A $10,000 holding at the start of that month was worth about $7,860 at the end. Airbnb's own news over those weeks does not explain it, so the fall needs a different explanation.
